transcript: one thing that I am a total sucker for is stories that center around super specific traditions and rituals and this riveting new play by Pulitzer winner Katori Hall is a perfect example of that The Blood Quilt is about four sisters who reunite after the ☠️ of their mother to engage in a quilting ritual that goes back centuries in their family so like I said I love stories about rituals but what I don't always love is this sort of family drama where it feels like a lot of the drama just comes from like yelling at each other and revealing secrets about the past in a way that it feels like we're kind of just backloading the plot instead of watching the plot happen right in front of us and yet in this case it really worked for me a big part of that is Lileana Blain-Cruz who I really think is one of the most skilled directors in the industry right now and in this production she just does a fantastic job calibrating the drama so that even when it is explosive and theatrical it never feels too melodramatic part of that is that they've assembled this rock solid ensemble of actors who are likewise just totally dropped into their characters and in sync with each other and listening and responding so I was swept up in a in a way that I am often not when I'm watching families bicker on stage but of course it wasn't just the direction Katori Hall deserves credit here too, obviously I love the way she uses this quilting ritual to kind of metaphorically mirror the relationship between the sisters themselves and going back to what I said before about how a lot of these plays feel like we're backloading the plot instead of watching the plot I think Katori Hall does a great job establishing that reckoning with your past is in many ways the core subject matter of the play by contrast I think a lot of playwrights use that sort of device as a means to a different end because they don't know how else to write a plot that takes place in one room having said that I do still think that in the hands of the wrong director this play could still slip into that fakey melodrama territory a little too easily but like I said Lileana Blain-Cruz absolutely nails it in either case I would definitely recommend checking out The Blood Quilt at Lincoln Center before it closes on December 29th
reasoning: Creator praises the direction, ensemble, and playwright's craft, overcoming his usual skepticism of family drama plays. Clear recommendation with minor caveat about the material in other hands.
